sections.heading: 1. A Forest is a System
points: A **forest** is a self-sustaining **ecosystem** of trees, plants, animals, microbes and their non-living surroundings.
It is called **'our lifeline'** because it gives **oxygen, clean air, water, food, timber, medicines** and homes to wildlife.
The forest has **layers**: tall trees form the **canopy** (top); shorter trees the **understorey**; below are shrubs and herbs; the ground has **decomposing litter**.

sections.heading: 2. Interdependence and Food Chains
points: **Producers** = green plants (make food); **consumers** = animals (herbivores, carnivores); **decomposers** = microbes and fungi (break down dead matter).
A **food chain** links who eats whom: e.g. **grass → deer → tiger**.
Many food chains interlink to form a **food web**.
**Decomposers** convert dead plants/animals into **humus**, enriching the soil — recycling nutrients.

sections.heading: 3. The Forest and the Balance of Nature
points: Forests maintain the **oxygen–carbon dioxide balance** (a 'green lung'): plants **release oxygen** and **absorb carbon dioxide**.
Forests **conserve water** and prevent **floods and soil erosion** (roots hold soil; canopy slows rain).
They influence **rainfall and climate** and are a huge store of **biodiversity**.
Nothing is wasted in a forest — it is a **dynamic, self-renewing** system.

sections.heading: 4. Protecting Forests
points: **Deforestation** (cutting forests) causes loss of wildlife, soil erosion, floods, and **more carbon dioxide** (global warming).
Forests are a **renewable** resource **only if used wisely**; they take a long time to grow.
Conservation: **afforestation (planting trees)**, protected areas, and community efforts.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Forest = self-sustaining ecosystem; layers: canopy (top), understorey, shrubs, forest floor.
Producers (plants) → consumers (animals) → decomposers (microbes/fungi → humus).
Food chain: grass → deer → tiger; many chains = food web.
Forests maintain O₂–CO₂ balance, conserve water, prevent floods & soil erosion.
Deforestation → wildlife loss, erosion, floods, more CO₂; remedy = afforestation.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Decomposers** (microbes, fungi) recycle nutrients by forming **humus** — vital to the forest.
In a food chain, the **arrow points from the eaten to the eater** (grass → deer → tiger).
Forests keep the **oxygen–carbon dioxide balance** (release O₂, absorb CO₂).
**Deforestation increases carbon dioxide** and worsens floods and soil erosion.
